scope: Fine-grained node and directed-edge types for cloud data attack and exposure paths.
normalization: Unicode casefold; spaces and hyphens become underscores; aliases are explicit and frozen.

node_types.definition: An actor originating outside the controlled cloud trust boundary.
A generic cloud principal when a more specific identity subtype is unsupported.
A machine, service-account, managed-identity, or workload principal.
An assumable or assignable cloud authorization role.
A password, key, token, certificate, or equivalent authentication material.
An IAM, RBAC, ACL, resource, or equivalent authorization policy.
A network, endpoint, firewall, security group, or reachability boundary.
A VM, container, function, cluster, or other execution resource.
A cloud control-plane or managed service endpoint.
A relational, document, key-value, graph, warehouse, or equivalent database service.
An object-storage bucket, container, or equivalent storage service.
A managed secret, key, vault, or configuration-secret store.
A table, object, record set, file, backup, snapshot, or other data-bearing object.
A queue, topic, stream, or messaging resource.
A non-cloud or separately administered system participating in the path.
A generic cloud resource when a finer type is unsupported by evidence.

edge_types.definition: Authenticates a principal to a service or identity plane.
Uses credential material to act as or reach another principal/resource.
Assumes, activates, or exchanges into a role.
Acts as another principal through delegation or impersonation.
Creates or changes an authorization relationship.
Represents an evidenced authorization capability without claiming it was exercised.
Changes IAM, RBAC, ACL, trust, or resource policy.
Represents network-level reachability without claiming successful application access.
Lists, describes, discovers, or otherwise enumerates a target.
Invokes a cloud API, function, job, command, or service operation.
Executes code, a command, workload, or job.
Exploits a vulnerability or unsafe behavior to advance the path.
Establishes an application or service connection.
Creates a cloud resource used by the path.
Changes non-policy configuration that advances or enables the path.
Accesses data when read/write direction cannot be established.
Reads, downloads, queries, or retrieves data.
Writes, inserts, uploads, or modifies data.
Stages or aggregates data in preparation for movement or impact.
Moves or copies data between controlled resources or services.
Moves data outside its authorized trust or administrative boundary.
Deletes or destroys data, backups, snapshots, or recovery material.
Encrypts data in a way that creates availability or extortion impact.
Disables, removes, or inhibits recovery mechanisms.
Publishes data or a message to a queue, topic, stream, or external endpoint.
Links a data object to an evidenced sensitivity or classification.
A directly observed cloud operation whose higher-level path semantics remain unspecified.
